atoms.text: This guide describes how to let the Tallyflow query engine read raw event logs from the bucket acme-event-logs and write query results to the bucket acme-query-results. Tallyflow runs queries under the IAM role TallyflowQueryRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to that role, and the bucket policies of both buckets are left unchanged. Create a policy statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-event-logs/raw/* and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-event-logs, with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-query-results/output/*, plus s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads and s3:GetBucketLocation on the results bucket itself. Attach the policy to TallyflowQueryRole and confirm that no bucket policy statement references the role. Run a test query that scans one day of logs, then verify that a CSV result object named with the query ID appears under output/. If the query fails with AccessDenied, check the resource ARNs in the role's attached policy, because no other policy contributes permissions.

This guide describes how to let the Tallyflow query engine read raw event logs from the bucket acme-event-logs and write query results to the bucket acme-query-results. Tallyflow runs queries under the IAM role TallyflowQueryRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through a statement in each bucket's resource-based policy, and the role has no S3 permissions in its own identity-based policies. In the policy of acme-event-logs, add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/TallyflowQueryRole and that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-event-logs/raw/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket, with an s3:prefix condition limited to raw/*. In the policy of acme-query-results, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-query-results/output/*, plus s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket itself. Save both policies and confirm that no policy attached to the role mentions either bucket. Run a test query that scans one day of logs, then verify that a CSV result object named with the query ID appears under output/. If the query fails with AccessDenied, check the Principal ARN and resource ARNs in the bucket policies, because no other policy contributes permissions.

This guide covers giving the Pipewright ETL runner access to a landing bucket and a curated bucket. Pipewright authenticates as the IAM user pipewright-runner, which uses access keys stored in the runner's secrets file. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that user, and neither bucket's policy is modified. The policy needs s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on acme-landing, limited to the prefix incoming/csv/, because the job reads nightly CSV exports from that location. It also needs s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-curated/warehouse/* so the job can write Parquet partitions, and s3:DeleteObject on the same path so it can replace partitions when a night is re-run. Attach the policy directly to pipewright-runner or to a group that contains the user. Start a dry run against a single date partition and confirm that Parquet files appear under warehouse/ with the expected date key. If the run reports AccessDenied on a delete, check that the s3:DeleteObject action is present in the user's policy, since the buckets contribute no permissions of their own.

This guide covers giving the Pipewright ETL runner access to a landing bucket and a curated bucket. Pipewright authenticates as the IAM user pipewright-runner in account 111122223333, which uses access keys stored in the runner's secrets file. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policies, and the user has no S3 permissions in any identity-based policy. In the policy of acme-landing, add a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/pipewright-runner that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, limited to the prefix incoming/csv/, because the job reads nightly CSV exports from that location. In the policy of acme-curated, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-curated/warehouse/* so the job can write Parquet partitions, and s3:DeleteObject on the same path so it can replace partitions when a night is re-run. Do not attach any S3 policy to the user or to its groups. Start a dry run against a single date partition and confirm that Parquet files appear under warehouse/ with the expected date key. If the run reports AccessDenied on a delete, check that s3:DeleteObject appears in the acme-curated bucket policy statement, since the user's own policies contribute no permissions.

This guide explains how to give the Rivulet stream aggregator access to a checkpoint bucket and an aggregates bucket. Rivulet workers assume the IAM role RivuletWorkerRole, and each worker reads window checkpoints and writes five-minute aggregate files. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policies are not edited. Allow s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stream-state/checkpoints/* so workers can recover and compact their state. Allow s3:ListBucket on acme-stream-state with a prefix condition for checkpoints/. In a separate statement, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stream-aggregates/windows/* for the aggregate output. Attach the policy to RivuletWorkerRole and restart one worker to confirm that it reads its last checkpoint. After the next window closes, verify that an aggregate object appears under windows/ with the window start time in its key. A missing checkpoint listing usually means the s3:ListBucket statement lacks the prefix condition or the role's policy was not attached.

This guide explains how to give the Rivulet stream aggregator access to a checkpoint bucket and an aggregates bucket. Rivulet workers assume the IAM role RivuletWorkerRole in account 111122223333, and each worker reads window checkpoints and writes five-minute aggregate files. Access is granted only through resource-based bucket policies, and no S3 statements are added to the role's identity-based policies. In the policy of acme-stream-state, add a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RivuletWorkerRole that allows s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stream-state/checkpoints/* so workers can recover and compact their state. In the same statement set or a second one, allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for checkpoints/. In the policy of acme-stream-aggregates, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stream-aggregates/windows/* for the aggregate output. Restart one worker to confirm that it reads its last checkpoint. After the next window closes, verify that an aggregate object appears under windows/ with the window start time in its key. A missing checkpoint listing usually means the s3:ListBucket statement in the state bucket policy lacks the prefix condition or names the wrong role ARN.

This guide describes how to let an analyst run ad-hoc queries in the Notebookd workspace and export results to a team bucket. The analyst signs in as the IAM user mchen, and Notebookd uses that user's credentials for every read and write. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to mchen, and the bucket policy of acme-analyst-exports is not changed. The policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the shared dataset bucket acme-datasets under the prefix public-sales/. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analyst-exports/mchen/* so exports can only be written to the analyst's own folder. Attach the policy to mchen and remove any broader S3 policy that was previously attached. In a notebook, run a query that reads one table from public-sales/ and exports the result as a CSV file. Confirm that the object appears under mchen/ and that an attempt to write to another analyst's folder returns AccessDenied. If reads fail, check for a missing s3:ListBucket statement, which Notebookd needs in order to enumerate table partitions.

This guide describes how to let an analyst run ad-hoc queries in the Notebookd workspace and export results to a team bucket. The analyst signs in as the IAM user mchen in account 111122223333, and Notebookd uses that user's credentials for every read and write. Access is granted only by statements in bucket policies, and no S3 permissions are attached to mchen directly or through a group. In the policy of acme-datasets, add a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/mchen that allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket under the prefix public-sales/. In the policy of acme-analyst-exports, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analyst-exports/mchen/* so exports can only be written to the analyst's own folder. Remove any broader S3 policy previously attached to the user. In a notebook, run a query that reads one table from public-sales/ and exports the result as a CSV file. Confirm that the object appears under mchen/ and that an attempt to write to another analyst's folder returns AccessDenied. If reads fail, check for a missing s3:ListBucket statement in the datasets bucket policy, which Notebookd needs in order to enumerate table partitions.

This guide covers access for the Ledgerline reporting service, which reads transaction exports and writes monthly reports. Ledgerline runs in account 444455556666 as the IAM role LedgerlineReportRole, and the transaction exports bucket acme-finance-exports and the reports bucket acme-finance-reports are in the same account. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and both bucket policies remain unchanged. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-exports/transactions/* and s3:ListBucket on acme-finance-exports with a prefix condition for transactions/. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-reports/monthly/* so the service can write one CSV and one summary file per month. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, so that a published report cannot be overwritten without versioning history. Attach the policy and trigger a report run for the previous month. Verify that both output files appear under monthly/ with the year and month in their keys. If the run fails when listing inputs, confirm that the role's policy includes the bucket-level ListBucket statement in addition to the object-level read statement.

This guide covers access for the Ledgerline reporting service, which reads transaction exports and writes monthly reports. Ledgerline runs in account 444455556666, while the transaction exports bucket acme-finance-exports and the reports bucket acme-finance-reports belong to account 777788889999. Access is granted only by statements in the two bucket policies, whose Principal is the account ID arn:aws:iam::444455556666:root. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-exports/transactions/* and s3:ListBucket on acme-finance-exports with a prefix condition for transactions/. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-finance-reports/monthly/* so the service can write one CSV and one summary file per month. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, so that a published report cannot be overwritten without versioning history. Because the Principal is an account ID, the role LedgerlineReportRole needs no S3 grant in its own policies for this access to work. Trigger a report run for the previous month and verify that both output files appear under monthly/ with the year and month in their keys. If the run fails when listing inputs, confirm that the exports bucket policy includes the bucket-level ListBucket statement in addition to the object-level read statement.

This guide explains how to give the Featurekiln job runner access to clickstream data and a feature output location. Featurekiln jobs run under the IAM role FeaturekilnJobRole and read gzip-compressed clickstream files before writing feature tables as Parquet. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy of acme-clickstream and acme-features is not modified. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-clickstream/events/year=2026/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for events/year=2026/. Allow s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on acme-features for the path tables/*, because large Parquet files are uploaded in multiple parts. Attach the policy to FeaturekilnJobRole and submit a job that processes a single day. Check that the feature table files appear under tables/ and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain after completion. Also add a lifecycle rule on acme-features that expires incomplete uploads after seven days. If large files fail while smaller ones succeed, verify that the multipart actions are present in the role's policy.

Featurekiln jobs run under the IAM role FeaturekilnJobRole in account 111122223333 and read gzip-compressed clickstream files before writing feature tables as Parquet. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket policies of acme-clickstream and acme-features, and the role has no S3 statements in its identity-based policies. In the policy of acme-clickstream, add a statement with Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FeaturekilnJobRole that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-clickstream/events/year=2026/* and s3:ListBucket with a prefix condition for events/year=2026/. In the policy of acme-features, add a statement with the same Principal that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads for the path tables/*, because large Parquet files are uploaded in multiple parts. Submit a job that processes a single day. Check that the feature table files appear under tables/ and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain after completion. Also add a lifecycle rule on acme-features that expires incomplete uploads after seven days. If large files fail while smaller ones succeed, verify that the multipart actions are present in the acme-features bucket policy.

This guide describes how to let the Logsieve anomaly detector read compressed access logs and write job results. Logsieve is invoked by the IAM role LogsieveScanRole in account 111122223333 and scans one hour of logs per job. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy on that role, and no statement is added to the bucket policy of acme-access-logs or acme-scan-results. The policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-access-logs/web/* and s3:ListBucket on acme-access-logs with a prefix condition for web/. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scan-results/anomalies/* so each job can write a JSON findings file and a manifest file. Attach the policy to LogsieveScanRole, then start a job covering a single hour of traffic. Confirm that the findings file and manifest appear under anomalies/ with the job ID in the key name. Review the role's attached policies if the job completes but writes no output, since the scan itself can succeed while the write statement is missing. The bucket policies play no part in this access.

This guide describes how to let the Logsieve anomaly detector read compressed access logs and write job results. Logsieve is invoked from account 888899990000, and the buckets acme-access-logs and acme-scan-results are owned by account 111122223333. Access is granted only by statements in the two bucket policies, with Principal arn:aws:iam::888899990000:root, so any role or user in that account may use the grants if its own policies also permit the actions. In the policy of acme-access-logs, allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-access-logs/web/* and s3:ListBucket with a prefix condition for web/. In the policy of acme-scan-results, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scan-results/anomalies/* so each job can write a JSON findings file and a manifest file. Start a job covering a single hour of traffic. Confirm that the findings file and manifest appear under anomalies/ with the job ID in the key name. Review the acme-scan-results bucket policy if the job completes but writes no output, since the scan itself can succeed while the write statement is missing. The identity-based policies of the invoking role are not part of this guide.

This guide covers access for the Gaugeworks data quality service, which reads input tables and writes validation reports. Gaugeworks runs as the IAM role GaugeworksCheckRole and checks tables stored as Parquet in the bucket acme-warehouse. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy of acme-warehouse is not changed. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse/tables/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for tables/. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-warehouse/quality-reports/* so the service can write one JSON report and one rejected-rows file per check. Because input and output share a bucket, scope the write statement to quality-reports/ only, so checks cannot modify source tables. Attach the policy and run a check against one table. Confirm that the report appears under quality-reports/ and that an attempted write to tables/ is denied. If the service cannot list partitions, verify that the policy's s3:ListBucket statement uses the bucket ARN and not an object ARN.
